The research brief is written to `/Users/mdostal/Documents/work/pantheon/minerva/.pHive/epics/fix-startrun-heimdall-routing/docs/research-brief.md`.

Beyond relaying the raw findings, I read the actual source (`src/driver.ts`, `src/dispatch.ts`, `src/agnostic-plan-driver.ts`, `src/run-manager.ts`, `src/kickoff-engine.ts`, `src/cleanup-ledger.ts`, `src/errors.ts`, `src/driver-route.test.ts`) to pin exact line numbers and surface several load-bearing facts not in the raw material:

- `SubagentDriver` (`driver.ts:670`) and `ForkedHiveDriver` (`driver.ts:871`, `:949`) call the same unguarded `resolveRuntimeRoute()` — the bug isn't `SpawnDriver`-exclusive.
- `submitAnswers` (`kickoff-engine.ts:418`) hits the identical path via `driverForRecord()`'s default fallback.
- `runTurnResumable()` (`kickoff-engine.ts:90-101`) only retries `TurnTimeoutError` — a routing failure is never retried.
- `driver-route.test.ts:97-103` already asserts today's fail-loudly behavior as intentional, so this isn't an untested oversight — a fix must consciously rewrite that test.
- `errors.ts` has only 5 `ErrorCode` values, none fit for "internal dependency failure," which bounds how the `UNKNOWN_METHOD` fix can be shaped.
- `cleanup-ledger.ts` already provides an AD-4-compliant `abortRun`/`recordCleanup` mechanism (record + signal, never delete) that `startRun`'s failure path could hook into rather than needing new infrastructure — but AD-4 explicitly forbids deleting workspace/state directly, which constrains any "cleanup" design.

The brief follows the required section order (Summary, Key files & surfaces, Patterns & conventions, Constraints, Risks, Open questions, Recommendation) with the Recommendation section clearly marked as synthesis, every non-obvious claim cited to file/line, and six flagged open questions rather than invented answers (correct Heimdall task-type value, fail-open-vs-fail-fast design intent, cleanup scope, whether an ADR already covers the divergence, epic scope boundary across drivers, and the target shape of the debuggability fix).
